title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 73–75): Grothendieck is studying the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. Here M^∞ is the boundary, stratified by stable dual graphs (MD-graphs). The point being proved is a connectivity statement for maximal degenerations. Take any two maximally degenerate strata (points of M^∞_{g,ν}). They should be joinable by a chain of points in which consecutive ones lie on a common boundary component, i.e. a common 1-dimensional stratum.

The previous page settles g ≥ 1 by finding common specializations. In genus 0 (with card I ≥ 6 in the case treated there) it shows that every case b) specializes to a 'caterpillar' configuration b″). That is a chain of trivalent vertices whose two end vertices each carry two marked points and whose inner vertices each carry one.

This page finishes the genus-0 case.
- A caterpillar is determined by a total order (c_1,…,c_ν) on I. The order is defined only up to transposing the first two elements and the last two, since those pairs sit on the same end vertex.
- Adjacent transpositions generate the symmetric group. So it suffices to show that two orders differing by an adjacent transposition c_i ↔ c_{i+1} give points lying on a common component.
- This is immediate. Contract the edge joining the vertices carrying c_i and c_{i+1}. The result is the graph (c_1,c_2) c_3 … c_{i-1} (c_i,c_{i+1}) c_{i+2} … c_ν, which has one 4-valent vertex and so is a 1-dimensional stratum ≅ M_{0,4}.
- Its closure P^1 has three boundary points. Two of them are the caterpillars …c_{i-1} c_i c_{i+1} c_{i+2}… and …c_{i-1} c_{i+1} c_i c_{i+2}…; both are specializations of it ('en contractant l'arête qui joint c_i et c_{i+1}, OK').

Hence the graph whose vertices are maximal degenerations and whose edges are 1-dimensional strata is connected for g = 0. This combines with the earlier g ≥ 1 argument. It serves the later construction (§9, next page) of the modular groupoids / Teichmüller tower. There, connectivity of base points at infinity, with 'elementary moves' through M_{0,4}-type strata, underlies the two-level generation principle.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is complete modulo trivial edge cases. Transpositions at i = 1 or i = ν−1 do not change the point. For i = 2 or i = ν−2, the contracted vertex carries three marked points plus one edge, which is still a 4-valent vertex, so the argument holds. Grothendieck does not spell these cases out, but they are harmless.

ideas.what: Connectivity of the graph of maximal degenerations of M̄_{0,ν} (0-dimensional boundary strata joined by 1-dimensional strata), via caterpillar trees indexed by total orders and adjacent transpositions realized inside M_{0,4} strata
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of the 1-skeleton of the boundary stratification of M̄_{0,n} (genus-0 pants graph / associahedral A-moves); caterpillar/comb trees
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Thurston (1980) for pants-decomposition complexes; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000) for the Teichmüller tower/pants complex; folklore in genus 0 (Kapranov, Keel)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3: Teichmüller tower, 'jeu de Lego', the two-level principle, and paths between base points at infinity. This specific proof does not appear there.

ideas.what: Reduction of connectivity to adjacent transpositions generating S_ν, each realized by contracting one edge to a 4-valent vertex
ideas.modern_name: Elementary 'A-move' (associativity move) in M_{0,4}; generation of S_n by adjacent transpositions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but routine combinatorial lemma: a connectivity argument for maximal degenerations in genus 0. It is well known today through the pants-graph and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps work and through elementary M̄_{0,n} combinatorics. Its interest is mainly historical, as an early worked-out step toward the Esquisse's Lego/two-level philosophy.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'diagrammes qui se déduisent ; [ils sont] uniques' rather than 'dans ce cas[?]'.
Lines 2–4 are better read as 'puis on a donné un ordre total sur I, (défini à transposition près des deux premiers et des deux derniers)'.
'= composante commune' should read 'à composante commune' (points lying on a common component).
Lines 9–11 likely read 'deux ordres totaux déduits l'un de l'autre par transposition de deux éléments consécutifs c_i, c_{i+1} ont leurs pts à composante commune'.
'les deux ... généralisations' is likely 'les deux sont des spécialisations de'. The context (contracting an edge gives the more general stratum) supports this.
In the diagram, the last label is c_ν, and the 'c' under the first dot is presumably the vertex marking.
